concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: game playable character design comparison sheet, concept 01, not animation sheet.
Input images: image1 is Ari identity/size reference (use ONLY the upright first sprite as the small original character); images2 and3 are phoenix family style references ONLY, do not reproduce their fire/ice aura or summon poses.
Primary request: design an ADULT ROCK PHOENIX transformation of Ari, a directly player-controlled bird who runs on the ground and dashes with a heavy body. Round granite guardian: rounded granite boulder chest, short sturdy legs and massive overlapping stone feather plates; wide but compact folded wings; three thick stone tail plumes. Warm light gray and cream stone, tiny pale gold seams. Heavy and lovable, the most physically grounded version.
Compose one clean landscape sheet on a flat desaturated charcoal background. Upper/central comparison: one SMALL original Ari at left standing on same baseline as one rock phoenix at right. Preserve Ari's exact pale pink egg body, curl on forehead, black eyes, yellow beak, cream feet and tiny wings from image1. No redesign of small Ari. Adult top-of-head height exactly 1.5 times small Ari foot-to-head height, excluding wings; don't make it a huge boss. Both face slightly right, full body uncut, identical pixel density/outline language. Keep at least 12% whitespace.
Bottom right: a separate smaller action study of SAME rock phoenix leaning low and dashing right, wings folded as stone shoulders, one rear foot pushing ground, compact dust not flames. Not another variant. Adult main stance must have planted legs and articulated solid wings suitable for real walking and dashing, NOT a floating summon VFX. Refined pixel-art edges and dark readable contours matching the current game, limited clustered shading, no photorealistic texture. Keep eyes and face kind and identifiable.
No text, numbers, watermark, frame, weapons, fire, lava, ice, surrounding magical aura. No sprite grid. This is a scale comparison concept sheet, not final production sprites.
